title: PKU manufacturers & companies
source_note: Corporate/market map of companies across the PKU value chain (medical food, protein-substitute formula, drug, and services). Compiled from company sites, press releases, M&A coverage, and PitchBook/Crunchbase-style profiles. Revenue figures are parent-level or divisional where noted; segment-specific PKU revenue is rarely disclosed and is marked 'estimate' or 'unknown'. Not investment advice.

records.scale_note: Nutricia is the core of Danone's Specialized Nutrition division; medical-nutrition unit revenue reported around $1.6B (Growjo estimate). Danone group revenue ~EUR 27B (2024).
records.ma_note: Nutricia acquired by Danone via the EUR 12.3B purchase of Royal Numico in 2007; delisted from Amsterdam exchange end of 2007. SHS International (metabolic specialist) rolled in earlier.
records.notes: Category originator (first PKU product, 1956) and global volume leader in metabolic formula; one of the two food conglomerates (with Nestle) that dominate PKU protein substitutes.

records.scale_note: At acquisition (2010) had ~CHF 40M annual sales; now embedded in Nestlé Health Science (a multi-billion-CHF division). Segment-level revenue not separately disclosed.
records.ma_note: Liverpool-based; acquired by Nestlé (Nestlé Health Science) in August 2010. In 2021 Vitaflo acquired Dr. Schär's inborn-errors-of-metabolism protein-substitute product line and its Rosbach, Germany plant.
records.notes: Nestlé's entry vehicle into inherited metabolic disorders; the #2 pole of the formula duopoly opposite Danone/Nutricia, and an active consolidator of smaller metabolic lines.

records.scale_note: Small subsidiary; standalone revenue not disclosed. Ajinomoto group revenue ~JPY 1.4T. Cambrooke deal value not publicly detailed.
records.ma_note: Founded 2000 by PKU parents Lynn & David Paolella (as Cambrooke Foods). Backed by Galen Partners and Seventure Partners; acquired by Ajinomoto (via Ajinomoto North America) in Nov 2017; renamed Ajinomoto Cambrooke in April 2019.
records.notes: Pioneered Glytactin/GMP (glycomacropeptide) intact-protein medical food, differentiating from amino-acid formulas; gives Japanese food-and-amino-acid giant Ajinomoto a PKU foothold.

records.scale_note: European leader in gluten-free; group revenue estimated in the several-hundred-million-EUR range (private, not disclosed). Mevalia is its low-protein/metabolic brand.
records.ma_note: Launched Mevalia low-protein line in 2013. Divested its inborn-errors-of-metabolism protein-substitute (amino-acid mixture) product line and Rosbach plant to Nestlé/Vitaflo in 2021, retaining Mevalia low-protein foods.
records.notes: Independent private counterweight to the conglomerates on the low-protein food side; exited the higher-margin formula/protein-substitute niche to Nestlé while keeping staple low-protein foods.

records.scale_note: Abbott Nutrition division revenue ~$8B (parent Abbott ~$40B+ total). PKU line (Phenex-1/-2) is a small metabolic-formula niche within it; PKU-specific revenue unknown.
records.ma_note: No recent PKU-specific M&A; Phenex is a longstanding metabolic medical-food line under Abbott's broader nutrition franchise (Similac/Ensure/PediaSure).
records.notes: Large diversified US player present in PKU via amino-acid formulas, but PKU is peripheral to its mainstream nutrition business.

records.scale_note: Reckitt acquired Mead Johnson for ~$16.6B in 2017. Mead Johnson (now Reckitt's Nutrition/MJN unit) multi-billion revenue; PKU (Phenyl-Free) line is a small legacy metabolic niche.
records.ma_note: Mead Johnson acquired by Reckitt Benckiser in 2017. Reckitt announced strategic review / plans to divest its Mead Johnson infant-nutrition business (2024-2025), which could change ownership of the Phenyl-Free line.
records.notes: Phenyl-Free is a historic PKU medical food; its parent's infant-nutrition arm is itself an M&A target, adding uncertainty to this small niche.

records.scale_note: Small privately held US medical-foods maker; revenue not disclosed. Not to be confused with UK-listed Applied Nutrition Plc (sports nutrition, unrelated).
records.ma_note: No notable M&A. Long-running independent supplier of PKU/MSUD formulas and protein-free foods/candies.
records.notes: Independent US niche player supplying metabolic formulas and low-protein/protein-free convenience products; competes on specialty SKUs rather than scale.

records.scale_note: Small German FSMP maker (founded 1999; Friedberg & Burgheim sites); revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: No notable M&A; independent. Involved in R&D on recombinant/Phe-free nutritional proteins.
records.notes: Independent European specialist in XPhe amino-acid mixtures and low-protein foods; innovator on next-gen protein substitutes.

records.scale_note: Small family firm (formed 1993); 100+ low-protein SKUs. Revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: Independent; entered US market via an exclusive distribution agreement with Pentec Health / ZOIA Pharma (2023).
records.notes: Independent UK low-protein food maker (Promin brand); reaches the US through distribution partnerships rather than being acquired.

records.scale_note: Small privately held specialty-food maker (est. 1962); revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: No notable M&A; long-standing independent.
records.notes: Independent low-protein/gluten-free food maker serving PKU and renal diets; broad free-from catalog, PKU is one of several use cases.

records.scale_note: Very small family company (founded 2001 by PKU parents); revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: Independent; Fate-branded low-protein mixes are distributed internationally (e.g., via Vitaflo/Nestlé networks in Australia).
records.notes: Micro-scale PKU-founder-run baking-mix maker; illustrates the long tail of family-run low-protein food businesses.

records.scale_note: Small privately held medical-nutrition company; revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: No notable M&A. Markets differentiated LNAA (large neutral amino acid) products (NeoPhe, PreKUnil).
records.notes: Independent niche player pursuing an alternative mechanism (LNAA Phe-blocking) rather than standard amino-acid formula.

records.scale_note: Micro-scale for-profit specialty foods; revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: No M&A; independent.
records.notes: Family-run low-protein convenience-food maker; another long-tail community-founded supplier.

records.scale_note: Total company revenue grew 13% YoY in FY2025; Palynziq ~$106M in Q2 2025 alone (+20% YoY). Kuvan revenue declining on generic erosion. Market cap in the tens of billions.
records.ma_note: Kuvan (sapropterin) lost US exclusivity in 2020 following a 2017 patent settlement with Par. Palynziq (pegvaliase) Phase 3 PEGASUS positive in adolescents; filings submitted H2 2025 to expand age eligibility (possible 2026 approval). Dropped a preclinical next-gen PKU candidate.
records.notes: The dominant PKU drug company: originator of both Kuvan and the only enzyme-substitution therapy (Palynziq). Now facing generic sapropterin and new entrants (PTC's sepiapterin, Otsuka's oral).

records.scale_note: Par is Endo's generics arm; sapropterin is one product in a broad generic portfolio. Product-level revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: First and (initially) only generic Kuvan: began shipping generic sapropterin dihydrochloride tablets and oral-solution powder on 1 Oct 2020 under a 2017 licensing settlement with BioMarin.
records.notes: First mover in generic sapropterin, opening price competition against BioMarin's Kuvan.

records.scale_note: Large global generics maker (group revenue >$3B); sapropterin is one niche generic. Manufacturer of record for the Javygtor branded generic.
records.ma_note: Launched generic sapropterin dihydrochloride powder for oral solution (2021) and tablets in the US; supplies the Javygtor product marketed by Cycle Pharmaceuticals.
records.notes: Major generic entrant compressing sapropterin economics; supply backbone behind branded-generic Javygtor.

records.scale_note: Private rare-disease specialty pharma; revenue not disclosed. Markets Javygtor in the US.
records.ma_note: Launched Javygtor (sapropterin dihydrochloride tablets and powder) in the US in October 2022 as a branded rare-disease offering.
records.notes: Rare-disease commercialization specialist using patient-support wrap-around services to compete in the sapropterin market against both BioMarin and pure generics.

records.scale_note: Private specialty/generic developer; revenue not disclosed.
records.ma_note: Zelvysia (sapropterin dihydrochloride) approved April 2025, a further sapropterin entrant expanding competition.
records.notes: Later sapropterin entrant, evidence of a crowding generic/branded-generic field around the off-patent BH4 molecule.

records.scale_note: Mid-cap rare-disease pharma (multi-hundred-million to ~$1B revenue range). Sephience approved in EU, US and Japan within six months (2025), a new global launch.
records.ma_note: Acquired sepiapterin (CNSA-001) via the $10M-upfront-plus-milestones acquisition of Censa Pharmaceuticals in June 2020; Sephience FDA and Japan approvals landed in 2025.
records.notes: First credible branded challenger to BioMarin's oral franchise: a BH4 precursor claiming a broader responder population than sapropterin; pricing expected Q1 2026.

records.ownership: public parent (Otsuka Holdings, Tokyo Stock Exchange)
records.scale_note: Large diversified pharma (group revenue >JPY 2T). Acquired PKU asset for up to ~$1.1B ($800M upfront + up to $325M milestones).
records.ma_note: Acquired Jnana Therapeutics (Aug, Sep 2024) for its lead PKU candidate JNT-517 (now repinatrabit), an oral SLC6A19 inhibitor; Otsuka initiated a global Phase 3 in 2025.
records.notes: Big-pharma bet on a first-in-class oral, diet-independent PKU mechanism; a leading threat to reshape the drug segment if Phase 3 succeeds.

records.ownership: VC-backed, now wholly owned subsidiary of Otsuka
records.scale_note: Clinical-stage biotech; acquired for up to ~$1.1B. Pre-acquisition VC-funded.
records.ma_note: Developed JNT-517 (oral SLC6A19 inhibitor) through Phase 1b/2 in PKU; acquired by Otsuka in 2024 (announced Aug, completed Sep).
records.notes: Origin of the leading oral PKU small molecule; exit validates VC interest in non-formula, diet-independent PKU therapeutics.

records.scale_note: Clinical-stage synthetic-biology biotech; effectively wound down.
records.ma_note: Discontinued the Synpheny-3 Phase 3 of SYNB1934 (labafenogene marselecobac) for PKU in early 2024 for likely futility; cut >90% of staff and ceased operations, pursuing strategic alternatives.
records.notes: Cautionary case: the engineered-bacteria (live biotherapeutic) approach to PKU failed in pivotal trials, removing a pipeline contender.

records.scale_note: Former gene-therapy biotech; PKU program discontinued.
records.ma_note: Discontinued its PKU gene-therapy/editing programs (HMI-102 / HMI-103) amid a tough financing environment; reverse-merged with Q32 Bio (Nov 2023), which pivoted the entity to autoimmune/inflammatory disease (Nasdaq: QTTB).
records.notes: Illustrates gene therapy's retreat from PKU on financing and technical risk; the corporate shell survives in an unrelated field.

records.scale_note: Small/mid-cap genomic-medicine company; PKU is not a current core program.
records.ma_note: Earlier disclosed a PKU gene-therapy program (ST-101, clinical plans ~2021); recent pipeline focuses on hemophilia A, Fabry and others, with PKU no longer a highlighted active clinical program.
records.notes: Former genomic-medicine entrant into PKU; largely deprioritized, reflecting the broader cooling of gene-therapy activity in the indication.

records.scale_note: Large mRNA company; PKU is an early-stage, non-front-runner pipeline program (mRNA-3283 / mRNA-3210).
records.ma_note: No PKU-specific M&A; PKU is an internal rare-disease mRNA program behind its lead metabolic candidate (methylmalonic acidemia).
records.notes: Represents the mRNA/enzyme-replacement approach (transient PAH expression) to PKU; optionality rather than a near-term commercial threat.
